title: How to Build a Lead Priority Queue in 60 Minutes
tldr: Grade every open lead A–F by Fit/Intent/Quality, rank by composite score (grade + overdue + recency), work top-down every morning. Start manual in Google Sheets; automate when you pass 200 leads.
why: Without a Priority Queue, your reps burn 30–90 minutes every morning deciding which lead to call first. That's ₹2–5 lakh per month in rep-hours wasted on triage, and 40–70% of Grade A leads going cold because they weren't called in the window. A priority system is the single highest-leverage behaviour change for most Indian B2B SMBs.
prerequisites: Access to your current lead list (CRM, Google Sheet, or CSV)
A rough ICP definition — even 3 attributes is enough (industry, geography, company size)
15 minutes of rep-shadow time to confirm current workflow

steps.heading: Export your open leads
steps.body: Pull every open lead from your existing system into a Google Sheet. Columns: name, phone, email, source, date added, last touch, stage.

steps.heading: Score each lead
steps.body: Add three columns: Fit (0–100), Intent (0–100), Quality (0–100). Score each lead by hand. Fit: ICP match. Intent: engagement recency. Quality: data completeness. 50 leads takes ~90 minutes the first time.

steps.heading: Assign grades
steps.body: Grade A: F≥65 + I≥60 + Q≥60. Grade B: F≥55 + I≥40 + Q≥50. Grade C: F≥40 + I≥25 + Q≥35. Grade F: Q<20. Add a Grade column.

steps.heading: Add rank score
steps.body: Formula: grade_points + overdue_bonus + recency_bonus. Grade weights: A=4000, B=3000, C=2000, D=500, F=-1. Overdue bonus: 800 if past SLA. Recency: up to 500.

steps.heading: Sort and distribute
steps.body: Sort by rank score descending. Top 30 per rep is the day's work. Share the sheet with reps Monday morning.

steps.heading: Measure for 2 weeks
steps.body: Track: % of Grade A contacted within SLA, ₹ recovered from previously-stale leads, Grade A conversion rate. Even a few reclaimed Grade A deals can add up to ₹1–3 lakh — the ROI that justifies the ritual.

steps.heading: Automate when manual breaks
steps.body: Past 200 leads, nobody updates the rank column religiously. Leadkaun automates this the same day — same formula, no spreadsheet maintenance.

commonMistakes: Sorting by recency instead of grade — defeats the whole point
Not decaying Intent over time — queue fills with stale Grade A leads
Working Grade F (junk) because they're 'easier to call' — burns time

faqs.q: How long before I see impact?
faqs.a: 2 weeks for measurable ₹ recovered; 60 days for cultural shift to 'queue-first' mornings.

faqs.q: What if my reps resist?
faqs.a: Don't mandate on day 1. Show the top rep's queue vs their gut-choices for a week. Data wins the argument.

faqs.q: Do I need a new CRM?
faqs.a: No. Start in Google Sheets. Automate only when manual breaks (usually around 200 leads or 3+ reps).

title: How to Set Up Lead Scoring for Your Sales Team
tldr: Define three scores (Fit, Intent, Quality), each 0–100, with transparent weights. Assign grades A–F using a fixed matrix. Start with Leadkaun defaults; customise per ICP only after 30 days of data.
why: Lead scoring is the decision layer on top of your pipeline — it tells your rep who to call first. Done right, it consistently converts Grade A leads better than working an ungraded pipeline. Done wrong (single-number black-box AI scores), reps don't trust the output and revert to gut feel.
prerequisites: A rough ICP — at minimum: target industry, geography, company size
30 days of historical closed-won deal data (or industry benchmarks if new)
Rep consensus on 3–5 intent signals that matter in your workflow

steps.heading: Define Fit weights
steps.body: Total 100 points across: industry (30), geography (20), business type (20), role (15), budget (15). Adjust within your team — a real estate team might weight geography higher.

steps.heading: Define Intent signals + weights
steps.body: Source baseline (referral 60, organic 50, paid ad 30). Call signal +15. WhatsApp reply +10. Meeting booked +25. Intent decay −3/day after threshold.

steps.heading: Define Quality gate
steps.body: Valid phone (30), email (15), company name (15), inquiry clarity (20), source reliability (10), junk penalty (up to −10). Quality < 20 = auto-Grade F.

steps.heading: Define grade matrix
steps.body: Grade A: F≥65 + I≥60 + Q≥60. Grade B: F≥55 + I≥40 + Q≥50. Grade C: F≥40 + I≥25 + Q≥35. Grade D: F≥20 + I≥10 + Q≥20. Grade F: Q<20.

steps.heading: Apply to existing leads
steps.body: Score every open lead by hand initially. Verify distribution: ~15% A, ~25% B, ~35% C, ~15% D, ~10% F is a healthy shape. If you're 50% A, your Fit weights are too lenient.

steps.heading: Communicate grades to reps
steps.body: Every rep should know what Grade A means and the SLA (24 hours). Post the grade matrix in the sales room.

steps.heading: Refine after 30 days
steps.body: Pull conversion data by grade. If Grade A converts <15%, weights need tightening. If Grade C converts >8%, weights are too strict.

commonMistakes: Using a single black-box AI score — reps don't trust what they can't explain
Setting Intent without decay — queue fills with permanently-stale Grade A leads
Tuning weights before seeing 30 days of data

faqs.q: Can I skip this and use Leadkaun's defaults?
faqs.a: Yes. Defaults are calibrated for Indian B2B SMBs and work for most teams on day one.

faqs.q: How often should I revisit my scoring setup?
faqs.a: Review your ICP every 90 days against conversion data by grade — are Grade A leads actually converting best? Adjust which industries, geographies and roles define your ICP if the mix has shifted. Don't fiddle more often, or you'll chase noise. The scoring weights themselves stay fixed and transparent.

faqs.q: Different weights per product line?
faqs.a: Yes on the Growth tier. Multi-product teams typically have 2–4 ICP profiles.

title: How to Run a Daily Morning Brief for Your Sales Team
tldr: Send each rep and manager a daily 8:30 AM IST email listing top Grade A leads, ₹ at risk today, and overdue follow-ups. Set the day before stand-up. Teams that adopt the ritual respond to Grade A leads far faster.
why: Morning Brief is the ritual that turns lead scoring and priority queues into a daily habit. A rep who opens their inbox to '₹1.8L to recover today — Priya, Rajesh, Mohan' has their day planned before coffee. A manager who opens their inbox to a per-rep rollup has the 1:1 already written. No dashboards opened, no stand-up debates — just action by 10 AM.
prerequisites: A graded lead system (hand-graded or via Leadkaun)
Each rep has an assigned lead pool
Email delivery infrastructure (Resend, SendGrid, or your CRM's email)

steps.heading: Define the rep brief structure
steps.body: Four sections: (1) Top 5 Grade A leads needing callback today, (2) ₹ at risk today, (3) Overdue follow-ups, (4) One-line reminder of the SLA.

steps.heading: Define the manager brief structure
steps.body: Per-rep rollup: ₹ at risk per rep, Grade A count per rep, overdue count per rep. One team total line at the top.

steps.heading: Compute ₹ at risk per lead
steps.body: Formula: avg deal value for grade × grade conversion rate. For a Grade A real-estate lead: ₹45L × 10% = ₹4.5L.

steps.heading: Schedule delivery at 8:30 AM IST
steps.body: Crontab: 0 3 * * 1-6 (UTC 3 AM = IST 8:30 AM, Monday–Saturday). Use Inngest or equivalent background job scheduler.

steps.heading: Frame copy as opportunity, not blame
steps.body: Rep version: '₹1.8L to recover today' not 'You missed ₹1.8L'. Manager version: per-rep numbers without commentary.

steps.heading: Include one-tap action links
steps.body: Every lead row has a 'Call now' link that opens the lead record. Reduces friction to zero.

steps.heading: Measure adoption for 2 weeks
steps.body: Track: email open rate (target 80%+), click-through rate to lead records (target 60%+), Grade A contact time shift (should drop 30–50%).

commonMistakes: Sending at 9 AM or later — misses the pre-standup window
Including too much data (more than 5 leads) — reps skim and miss signals
Using blame language in rep copy — reps tune out

faqs.q: Does Leadkaun send this automatically?
faqs.a: Yes. Morning Brief is a core feature — 8:30 AM IST, Monday–Saturday, every tier.

faqs.q: What if a rep is on leave?
faqs.a: Toggle 'out of office' in settings; Brief pauses for them.

faqs.q: Can I customise what managers see?
faqs.a: Yes — pick which per-rep metrics appear (₹ at risk, Grade A count, follow-up score, etc.).

title: How to Import 10,000 Leads from CSV Cleanly
tldr: Clean the CSV first (phone normalisation, duplicate detection, quality checks), then upload. Leadkaun handles 10,000 rows in under 60 seconds. Expect 20–40% of historical CSV data to be junk — that's normal.
why: CSV imports are where most 'CRM migrations' fail. Teams upload raw files, skip cleaning, then blame the tool when grading looks wrong. A 30-minute pre-upload audit doubles the quality of everything downstream — Fit scores, grade distributions, rep time spent.
prerequisites: Source CSV with at least: name, phone, email, source, date added
30 minutes for cleaning and validation
Access to your Leadkaun or target system

steps.heading: Dedupe on phone + name
steps.body: Indian phone formats vary (+91, leading 0, with spaces). Normalise to E.164 before dedup. Expect to drop 5–15% of rows.

steps.heading: Validate phone format
steps.body: Any row without a 10-digit Indian number (after normalisation) goes to a 'quarantine' sheet for manual review — usually junk or international.

steps.heading: Check company name sanity
steps.body: Filter for test strings ('asdf', 'test', 'xxx'). Flag rows without company name for manual ICP tagging.

steps.heading: Audit source reliability
steps.body: If 40%+ of a source's leads are junk, that source will bring down overall data quality. Consider excluding it from the import until source is fixed.

steps.heading: Upload via Leadkaun CSV import
steps.body: Drag-drop into the import UI. Leadkaun streams via Supabase Storage + Inngest batch worker (BATCH_SIZE=500). 10k rows finish in under 60 seconds.

steps.heading: Review Import Insight Screen
steps.body: Shows distribution by grade, source, and quality. If 60% are Grade F, the source data has a quality problem — don't blame the tool.

steps.heading: Run first Morning Brief on day 2
steps.body: Day 1 scoring is stabilising. Day 2 Morning Brief is the first real signal — check with reps whether the Grade A list looks right.

commonMistakes: Skipping the phone normalisation step — a large share of leads slip through as duplicates
Uploading without sanity-checking source reliability
Panicking when grade distribution looks unexpected — often reflects real data quality, not tool error

faqs.q: Can I undo an import?
faqs.a: Yes. Bulk-delete from the lead list with a date-added filter.

faqs.q: Does import overwrite existing data?
faqs.a: Dedup on phone — existing records get merged with new source tag logged.

faqs.q: Large imports hang Google Sheets?
faqs.a: For 50k+ row files, split into 10k-row chunks or use CSV directly.

title: How to Migrate from Zoho CRM to Leadkaun (in 2–4 Weeks)
tldr: Export from Zoho as CSV, audit (keep only live leads), onboard Leadkaun (same day), run parallel for 30 days, cut over, maintain Zoho read-only as archive. Total: 2–4 weeks for an SMB.
why: Most Indian SMBs leave Zoho because of rep-adoption failure, complexity, or the realisation that 'workflow CRM' isn't what they need — they need a Sales Behaviour OS. The migration itself is not the hard part; psychology is. Most teams think 'downgrading' when they should think 'rightsizing'.
prerequisites: Zoho admin access (export permission)
Clear business case: what ROI do you expect from Leadkaun
2–4 weeks of parallel-running bandwidth

steps.heading: Week 1: Export Zoho data
steps.body: Export Leads, Contacts, Accounts, Deals, Activity History as CSVs. Activity History is the big one — it carries every call, email, note.

steps.heading: Week 1: Audit
steps.body: Separate live leads (last 90 days activity) from archive. Most SMBs find 40–60% of Zoho data is stale. Migrate only live data.

steps.heading: Week 2: Onboard Leadkaun
steps.body: Same-day setup wizard. Pick industry (pre-configured ICP templates), import live leads via CSV, configure sales stages, create rep accounts.

steps.heading: Week 2: Parallel-run
steps.body: Keep Zoho running in read-only mode for safety. Reps use Leadkaun primarily; critical escalations can reference Zoho.

steps.heading: Week 3: Rep training + measurement
steps.body: 2-hour session per team. Show 3-tap logging, Priority Queue, Morning Brief. Baseline metrics: rep adoption rate, response time, ₹ recovered.

steps.heading: Week 4: Cutover
steps.body: Switch primary system. Maintain Zoho read-only for 90 days as fallback archive.

steps.heading: Day 90: Cancel Zoho
steps.body: If the 30-day parallel-run numbers hold (rep adoption >60%, response time halved, ₹ recovered > licence cost), cancel Zoho. Archive CSV export handles historical lookups.

commonMistakes: Migrating ALL historical data including 3-year-old stale leads — pollutes grade distribution
Cancelling Zoho before day 90 — no fallback if something breaks
Treating migration as a consulting engagement — SMBs don't need one

faqs.q: Can we migrate custom fields?
faqs.a: Yes. Zoho custom fields export cleanly; Leadkaun supports custom fields in lead records.

faqs.q: What happens to Zoho workflows?
faqs.a: Workflows don't migrate directly. Map each workflow to Leadkaun's equivalent (Priority Queue, Missed Opportunity, Follow-up Engine) — most are covered natively.

faqs.q: What about Zoho Books / Desk integration?
faqs.a: Keep Zoho Books / Desk if you use them. Leadkaun focuses on sales behaviour; Books / Desk are separate concerns.

title: How to Calculate ₹ at Risk for Your Sales Pipeline
tldr: Formula: (avg deal value × grade conversion rate) summed over overdue leads. For 10-rep Indian B2B SMB: typically ₹2–5 lakh weekly baseline. Compute manually for 2 weeks; automate with Leadkaun past that.
why: ₹ at risk is the single metric that turns sales reviews from activity debates into money conversations. It makes abstract 'overdue follow-up' concrete. Reps work differently when they see their own number. Managers coach differently. Reviews become conversations about recovery.
prerequisites: 90 days of closed-won deal data
Grade system in place (even manual)
Defined staleness SLA per grade

steps.heading: Compute avg deal value per industry
steps.body: Pull last 90 days of closed-won. Sum deal values ÷ count. Example: real estate team sees avg GCV ₹45 lakh.

steps.heading: Compute conversion rate per grade
steps.body: For each grade, count leads that closed ÷ total leads at that grade over same 90 days. Example: Grade A = 10%, Grade B = 5%, Grade C = 2%.

steps.heading: Compute ₹ per stale lead by grade
steps.body: Multiply avg deal value × conversion rate. Grade A real estate: ₹45L × 10% = ₹4.5L per stale lead.

steps.heading: Count stale leads by grade (per rep)
steps.body: Past SLA: Grade A 24h, Grade B 48h, Grade C 7d. Count per rep.

steps.heading: Sum: ₹ at risk = Σ(count × ₹ per grade)
steps.body: Example: 4 Grade A stale × ₹4.5L = ₹18L. Plus 8 Grade B × ₹2.3L = ₹18.4L. Total rep: ₹36.4L.

steps.heading: Surface in Monday manager review
steps.body: Open stand-up: 'Team: ₹4.2L at risk. Priya: ₹1.8L, Rajesh: ₹1.2L, Mohan: ₹1.2L.' Discuss recovery plans per rep.

steps.heading: Surface in rep Morning Brief
steps.body: Rep version: '₹1.8L to recover today — top 3: [lead names]'. Frame as opportunity, not blame.

commonMistakes: Using best-case deal values instead of medians — inflates the number, reps tune out
Shaming reps publicly with the number — destroys adoption
Tracking only ₹ at risk without pairing with ₹ recovered

faqs.q: What's a healthy ₹ at risk number?
faqs.a: ₹2–5 lakh/week for a 10-rep Indian B2B SMB is healthy steady-state. First week often shows ₹8–15 lakh because backlog accumulated.

faqs.q: Does Leadkaun automate this?
faqs.a: Yes. Missed Opportunity Engine runs continuously; Morning Brief surfaces the number daily.

faqs.q: What if deal values vary wildly?
faqs.a: Use median, not mean. If still too variable, segment by product line and compute per segment.

title: How to Log WhatsApp Conversations for Sales Tracking
tldr: Use 3-tap logging after each meaningful WhatsApp exchange: tap stage (first-reply / asking-questions / objection / meeting-booked / ghosted), tap intent (high / medium / low / negative), tap outcome (progressed / stuck / closed). Takes 10 seconds, feeds Intent Score.
why: Most Indian B2B first-contact happens on WhatsApp. If you're not logging those exchanges as signals, your scoring model is missing half the data — and Grade A leads are being under-weighted. 3-tap logging is the minimum-viable capture that keeps reps in flow.
prerequisites: Lead exists in your system (imported or manually added)
WhatsApp conversation has substantive content (not just 'hi')
Rep has Leadkaun mobile web or app access

steps.heading: Identify the lead in Leadkaun
steps.body: Open the lead record (search by phone number — Leadkaun matches Indian formats automatically).

steps.heading: Tap 'Log WhatsApp'
steps.body: Opens the 3-tap UI. No typing required.

steps.heading: Tap stage
steps.body: Options: First reply, Asking questions, Negotiating, Objection, Meeting booked, Ghosted. Pick the current state of the conversation.

steps.heading: Tap intent
steps.body: Options: High (green), Medium (amber), Low (grey), Negative (red). Your read of where the conversation is heading.

steps.heading: Tap outcome
steps.body: Options: Progressed, Stuck, Closed. What happened in this specific exchange.

steps.heading: Optional: attach screenshot
steps.body: For important objections or quotes, attach a screenshot. Skip for routine logging.

steps.heading: Confirm
steps.body: Taps flow into Intent Score: High = +10, Medium = +5, Low = 0, Negative = −10. Priority Queue re-ranks if the lead crosses a grade threshold.

commonMistakes: Logging every WhatsApp 'hello' — only log meaningful exchanges
Using 'High' intent for everything — calibrate to actual conversation quality
Forgetting to log 'ghosted' — without it, the lead's grade won't decay correctly

faqs.q: Do I need WhatsApp Business API?
faqs.a: No. 3-tap logging works with regular WhatsApp — rep types in WhatsApp, logs in Leadkaun.

faqs.q: Does Leadkaun auto-detect WhatsApp replies?
faqs.a: Not for regular WhatsApp. With WhatsApp Business API + a BSP (Gupshup, AiSensy), auto-detection is on roadmap.

faqs.q: Should a manager see the logs?
faqs.a: Yes — per-rep WhatsApp activity shows on the Rep Performance card. Aggregate view only; no access to screenshots without permission.

title: How to Bring Google Sheets Leads into Leadkaun (CSV Import)
tldr: Export your Google Sheet to CSV (File → Download → CSV), then import it in Leadkaun: Settings → Leads → Import, map columns (name, phone, email, source), and every row is graded A–F on import. Native background sheet sync is on the roadmap; CSV import is the live path today.
why: Most Indian SMBs live in Google Sheets — ad agencies dump lead data there weekly, WhatsApp enquiries get logged there manually. Today Leadkaun ingests those leads via CSV import (which handles Google Sheet exports directly), so you can start scoring and queuing without migrating your workflow. Native scheduled sync is planned; until then a CSV export takes seconds.
prerequisites: A Google Sheet with at least columns: name, phone
Access to download the sheet
A Leadkaun account (any tier, including Free)

steps.heading: Prepare your sheet
steps.body: Row 1 = headers. Required columns: name, phone. Recommended: email, source, date-added, initial-enquiry, company.

steps.heading: Export the sheet to CSV
steps.body: In Google Sheets: File → Download → Comma-separated values (.csv). One tab exports at a time — export each tab you need.

steps.heading: Open the importer
steps.body: In Leadkaun → Settings → Leads → Import. Upload the CSV; Leadkaun auto-detects headers.

steps.heading: Map columns
steps.body: Drag each CSV column to its Leadkaun field. Leadkaun pre-fills obvious matches (name, phone, email) and parses Indian amounts (₹1,50,000 / 2.5L / 1Cr).

steps.heading: Import and review
steps.body: Confirm the mapping and import. Every row is graded A–F on Fit × Intent × Quality as it lands, and phone-number dedup catches repeats automatically.

steps.heading: Re-import when the sheet updates
steps.body: When new rows accumulate, export and import again — dedup means re-importing the whole sheet only adds the genuinely new leads. (Scheduled auto-sync is on the roadmap.)

commonMistakes: Exporting the wrong tab — a .csv download captures only the active sheet tab
Not including a unique identifier column (phone) — dedup relies on it
Trying to import >100k rows at once — split into smaller files instead

faqs.q: Does Leadkaun sync my sheet automatically?
faqs.a: Not yet — native scheduled sync is on the roadmap. Today you import via CSV export, which takes a few seconds and dedups on phone number.

faqs.q: Will re-importing create duplicates?
faqs.a: No. Leadkaun dedups on phone number within your account, so re-importing an updated sheet only adds genuinely new leads.

faqs.q: Can I import multiple sheets?
faqs.a: Yes — import as many CSVs as you need. Set a different source tag per import to keep attribution clean.

title: How to Train Reps on a New Sales Tool (Without Losing a Week)
tldr: 2-hour hands-on session per team, not a half-day slideshow. Reps log 5 real leads during the session. Follow up with a daily 5-minute check-in for the first week, then weekly.
why: Most 'sales tool rollouts' fail at week 2 because training was a PowerPoint, not a practice session. Reps leave knowing the features but not the workflow. Two weeks later, 30% have reverted to their old tool. Practice-based training closes the reversion gap.
prerequisites: Tool onboarding done (Leadkaun onboarded, leads imported)
One manager + one power-user rep as champions
Team available for 2 uninterrupted hours

steps.heading: Pre-session: import each rep's 10 real leads
steps.body: Training works on real data, not demo data. Each rep has 10 of their own leads loaded in Leadkaun.

steps.heading: Session 1 (30 min): tour the UI
steps.body: Manager walks through: Priority Queue, lead record, 3-tap logging, Morning Brief preview. No slides.

steps.heading: Session 2 (60 min): practice logging
steps.body: Each rep logs 5 real interactions (call, WhatsApp, meeting) live, using their own leads. Manager spot-checks the logs.

steps.heading: Session 3 (30 min): Q&A + manager coaching demo
steps.body: Show a sample Monday review: ₹ at risk per rep, recovery plans. Reps see what 'performance' looks like in the new tool.

steps.heading: Day 1 after: first Morning Brief
steps.body: 8:30 AM IST, every rep gets their Brief. Manager sends a WhatsApp message: 'You're on the queue. Work top-down. I'll check in at 11.'

steps.heading: Week 1: daily 5-min check-ins
steps.body: Every morning at 10 AM, manager asks each rep one question: 'Top of queue today?'. Keeps workflow front-of-mind.

steps.heading: Week 2 onwards: weekly review
steps.body: Monday stand-up uses ₹ at risk as the opening metric. 1:1s reference queue adoption rate.

commonMistakes: Long slide-deck training — retention is under 10% after 2 days
Using demo data — reps don't see how it applies to their own work
No manager follow-up in week 1 — adoption collapses

faqs.q: What if a senior rep pushes back?
faqs.a: Don't fight. Let them run their own order for a week. Measure. Data wins if the tool works.

faqs.q: How long until it feels natural?
faqs.a: Two weeks of daily use. Don't measure adoption before that — it's still the learning curve.

faqs.q: What if a rep never adopts?
faqs.a: After 60 days of support and coaching, it's a discipline problem, not a tool problem. Performance review territory.

title: How to Track Property Enquiries for Indian Real Estate Teams
tldr: Grade every enquiry A–F within 5 minutes of arrival, surface Grade A in the Priority Queue for immediate callback, target a fast response window (minutes, not hours). Log WhatsApp + call outcomes in 3 taps. Track site visit conversion per source.
why: Real estate is the most response-time-sensitive vertical in Indian B2B — in Leadkaun's framing, Grade A enquiries reached quickly convert far better than 4-hour callbacks. A single missed site visit is ₹5–50 lakh in lost GCV. The workflow is simple; the discipline is what wins.
prerequisites: Active lead sources (99acres, MagicBricks, Housing.com, Facebook Ads, walk-ins)
Per-project ICP (luxury vs affordable, 2BHK vs 3BHK segments)
Team of 3+ reps assigned to enquiries

steps.heading: Ingest from every source
steps.body: 99acres + MagicBricks → export to Google Sheet → CSV import into Leadkaun (native Sheets sync on the roadmap). FB Ads → CSV upload. Walk-ins → manual entry (15 seconds).

steps.heading: Auto-grade on arrival
steps.body: Score on Fit (project match + location match + budget fit) + Intent (source baseline) + Quality (phone/email/inquiry). Grade A if all three strong.

steps.heading: Surface Grade A for immediate callback
steps.body: Priority Queue + instant alert to assigned rep. Rep aims to make first contact fast, while the enquiry is still hot.

steps.heading: Log every interaction in 3 taps
steps.body: Call outcome (interested / site visit booked / cold / wrong number). WhatsApp stage if engaged there. Site visit confirmation in one tap.

steps.heading: Follow-up cadence
steps.body: Grade A: 3 touches in day 1 (call, WA, call). Grade B: call + WA week 1. Grade C: weekly WA nurture.

steps.heading: Track conversion by source
steps.body: Source Truth card shows ₹ closed per source over last 90 days. Kill bad sources fast; double down on good ones.

steps.heading: Manager Monday review
steps.body: ₹ at risk per rep. Site visit conversion by source. Recovery plans for Grade A leads past SLA.

commonMistakes: Not normalising phone numbers — 20% duplicate leads from same enquirer
Calling freshest lead first instead of Grade A first
Losing WhatsApp thread when the rep changes shifts — always log the stage

faqs.q: What's the ideal response time?
faqs.a: Aim for under an hour on Grade A enquiries, 4–6 hours for Grade B. The faster a hot lead is reached, the better it tends to convert.

faqs.q: Can broker splits be tracked?
faqs.a: Yes — source attribution with commission splits configurable.

faqs.q: Does it integrate with 99acres directly?
faqs.a: Not natively in Phase 1 — Google Sheets export is the bridge. Native 99acres API on roadmap.

title: How to Score Student Enquiries for EdTech Admissions
tldr: Weight Fit heavily on course-match + programme-match. Intent decays faster during admissions season. Log WhatsApp parent replies in 3 taps — 80% of admissions conversations happen there. Target 2-hour response window for Grade A.
why: EdTech admissions is seasonal, WhatsApp-heavy, and parent-decision-driven. Counsellors carry 200–500 leads each — without a scoring system, 30 minutes of morning triage is burned before any calls happen. The right scoring model is the difference between 12 more admissions or 0 more admissions in a given cycle.
prerequisites: Course catalogue mapped (programme, fees, cohort start dates)
Admissions cycle calendar defined
Parent + student as primary + secondary contacts on lead records

steps.heading: Define course-specific ICP
steps.body: For each programme, weight Fit: course match (40), programme match (20), geography (15), parent engagement (15), budget signal (10).

steps.heading: Set admissions-cycle-aware Intent decay
steps.body: In-season (March–June): −2/day decay. Off-season: −0.5/day decay. Different cadence for different programmes.

steps.heading: Capture parent + student separately
steps.body: Lead record has primary contact (parent) and secondary (student). Either can engage on WhatsApp; both feed Intent.

steps.heading: Instant Grade A alert to counsellor
steps.body: New Grade A enquiry → push notification to assigned counsellor within 60 seconds. 2-hour SLA for first call.

steps.heading: 3-tap WhatsApp logging
steps.body: Parent replies: tap stage + intent + outcome. Feeds Intent Score. Threaded history visible to counsellor.

steps.heading: Course-completion follow-up cadence
steps.body: Grade A: counsellor call day 1, WhatsApp day 2, parent call day 4. Grade B: weekly nurture with course content.

steps.heading: Morning Brief per counsellor
steps.body: 8:30 AM IST email: '8 Grade A enquiries replied overnight. ₹6L in admissions at risk if not called by 11 AM.'

commonMistakes: Same scoring across programmes — a ₹5L MBA is not a ₹30k test prep
Not decaying Intent during cycle changes — June's Grade A is worthless in August
Counsellor cherry-picking instead of working queue top-down

faqs.q: Can we set different ICP per programme?
faqs.a: Yes on Growth tier. Engineering admissions, arts programmes, and PG programmes each get their own weights.

faqs.q: What about multi-course enquiries?
faqs.a: Lead record supports multiple product-interests. Primary interest drives the main grade.

faqs.q: What if a counsellor leaves mid-cycle?
faqs.a: One-click handover: lead record, history, WhatsApp thread, all transfer to new counsellor.

title: How to Run a Weekly Sales Review That Drives Recovery
tldr: 30-minute Monday review anchored on ₹ at risk and ₹ recovered — not calls made or meetings booked. Per-rep rollup opens the discussion. Each rep walks out with a specific ₹ recovery target for the week.
why: Most sales reviews are activity theatre — 'how many calls did you make?' — which doesn't move revenue. A review that starts with ₹ at risk per rep and ends with specific recovery plans shifts the entire team's incentives. Reps start owning outcomes, not just activity.
prerequisites: ₹ at risk metric running (manual or via Leadkaun Missed Opportunity Engine)
Grade system in place
30-minute Monday block with all reps + manager

steps.heading: Open with team ₹ at risk
steps.body: First line: 'Team ₹ at risk this week: ₹4.2 lakh. Last week: ₹3.1 lakh. Up or down — why?'

steps.heading: Per-rep rollup (3 min each)
steps.body: Each rep: their ₹ at risk, their ₹ recovered last week, top 3 stale leads they're targeting this week.

steps.heading: Identify stuck leads
steps.body: Any lead past Grade A SLA and uncontacted 3+ times goes into 'escalation' — manager takes over or reassigns.

steps.heading: Source-level pattern check (3 min)
steps.body: Any source with >30% junk or >50% stale? Flag for sales-marketing conversation.

steps.heading: Individual coaching moment (5 min)
steps.body: Pick one rep whose numbers shifted most (up or down). 5-minute public-facing coaching conversation.

steps.heading: Commitment round (5 min)
steps.body: Each rep states: '₹X I'll recover this week from [specific leads].' Write it down. Reference next Monday.

steps.heading: Close with Morning Brief reminder
steps.body: 'Your Brief hits at 8:30 tomorrow. Top of queue by 10 AM. See you Friday.'

commonMistakes: Opening with call volume — sets wrong frame for the whole meeting
Running over 30 minutes — reps tune out, lose the ritual
No public commitment round — nothing to follow up on next week

faqs.q: Monday or Friday?
faqs.a: Monday. Sets the week; doesn't just recap it.

faqs.q: What if a rep's ₹ at risk is high every week?
faqs.a: Diagnose: discipline issue (skip-queue), source issue (bad lead quality), or capacity issue (too many leads per rep)? Different fixes.

faqs.q: How long until culture shifts?
faqs.a: 8–12 weeks of consistent rhythm. Slower if reps resist; faster if leadership is visible in the ritual.

title: How to Get Sales Reps to Actually Follow Up
tldr: Follow-up isn't a motivation problem — it's a visibility and priority problem. Make the next action obvious (Priority Queue), auto-schedule follow-ups, put overdue Grade A/B leads in front of managers every morning, and coach on a per-rep follow-up score in weekly one-on-ones. Leadkaun runs alongside your CRM to surface and remind — reps still make the call.
why: Reps call the newest enquiry and forget the warm one that replied two days ago. Managers can't see who is slipping until the quarter misses. It looks like a discipline problem, but reps disengage when they can't tell which of 200 leads to work next and when 'did you follow up' is never measured. Fix the visibility and the behaviour follows.
prerequisites: Leads imported and graded A–F (ICP configured)
A manager who runs a consistent weekly rhythm
A follow-up SLA agreed per grade

steps.heading: Agree the follow-up SLA per grade
steps.body: Set the window each grade must be worked in — e.g. Grade A within 24 hours, B within 48 hours, C within a week. This is the SLA Leadkaun measures compliance against, so 'follow up' becomes concrete, not a vibe.

steps.heading: Make the next action obvious
steps.body: The Priority Queue ranks who to call next per rep and re-ranks as signals arrive, so reps work top-down instead of spending 30 minutes each morning deciding. No triage means no excuse.

steps.heading: Auto-schedule the follow-up
steps.body: A follow-up task is generated from each stage change and logged signal on a per-stage cadence; overdue ones are promoted and flagged automatically. The rep never has to remember to set a reminder.

steps.heading: Put overdue follow-ups in front of managers daily
steps.body: The 8:30 AM IST Morning Brief lists overdue Grade A/B leads and the ₹ at risk today. Managers see the slip the morning it happens, not at month-end.

steps.heading: Measure it per rep
steps.body: The follow-up score (completed ÷ completed + overdue) and the daily execution score turn 'did you follow up' into a number per rep, with response-compliance % against the SLA above.

steps.heading: Coach on the number, weekly
steps.body: In one-on-ones, review each rep's follow-up % and missed-recovery — not activity theatre like raw call counts. What gets measured and reviewed gets done.

commonMistakes: Chasing every lead equally — grade first, then work the queue, or reps drown
Measuring calls made instead of follow-up completion against the SLA
No manager rhythm — the score only changes behaviour if it's reviewed
Expecting automation to do the follow-up — Leadkaun surfaces and reminds; a rep still makes the call

faqs.q: Does Leadkaun message or call leads automatically?
faqs.a: No. It tells the rep who to follow up and when, and the rep logs the outcome in 3 taps (including WhatsApp via a manual 3-tap log). It does not auto-send messages.

faqs.q: What if a rep just ignores the queue?
faqs.a: The manager sees that rep's follow-up %, overdue count and response-compliance % in the Morning Brief and the rep scorecard — the gap is visible daily, so it gets coached.

faqs.q: How long until follow-up discipline sticks?
faqs.a: Usually a few weeks of consistent weekly review. Reps adopt fastest when the next action is obvious and the number shows up in their one-on-one.

title: How to Reduce Your Lead Response Time (Speed to Lead)
tldr: Cut the gap between a lead arriving and a rep making first contact. Get every lead into one ranked place, grade it on arrival, alert the assigned rep on new Grade A, hold a response SLA per grade, and start each day on the overnight hot leads. Track first-contact time per rep and size the gap with the missed-revenue calculator.
why: In Indian B2B the first team to reach a fresh enquiry usually wins it, yet most teams respond in hours. Slow response is rarely laziness — leads pile up across inboxes, WhatsApp and sheets with no triage, so a rep can't tell which of 200 to call first. Speed-to-lead on your best leads is the single highest-leverage metric most SMBs never measure.
prerequisites: Leads flowing into one place (CSV import or manual entry)
ICP configured so grading is meaningful
A response SLA agreed per grade

steps.heading: Get every lead into one ranked place
steps.body: Scattered inboxes and spreadsheets are why leads wait unseen. Centralise intake so nothing sits in a channel nobody is watching, and Leadkaun runs alongside your CRM rather than replacing it.

steps.heading: Grade on arrival
steps.body: Every lead is scored A–F across Fit, Intent and Quality in real time as it lands, so the hottest enquiries surface immediately instead of being buried under the newest ones.

steps.heading: Alert the assigned rep on a new Grade A
steps.body: A fresh Grade A drops to the top of that rep's Priority Queue with a notification, so the highest-intent lead is the obvious next call.

steps.heading: Hold a response SLA per grade
steps.body: Aim to reach Grade A within the hour, Grade B the same day, Grade C within the week. Leadkaun records speed-to-lead (time to first contact) on the first logged call or WhatsApp, so the SLA is measured, not hoped for.

steps.heading: Start the day on the hot leads
steps.body: The 8:30 AM IST Morning Brief lists the overnight Grade A leads to call first, so the morning starts with the buyers most likely to close today.

steps.heading: Measure and recover
steps.body: Track first-contact time per rep, and use the Missed Opportunity Engine's ₹-at-risk view plus the missed-revenue calculator to size what slow response is costing — then work the recovery queue.

commonMistakes: Treating all leads equally — grade first, then chase Grade A fast; slow on cold leads is fine
Measuring average response across all leads instead of Grade A specifically
Leaving leads in WhatsApp or a sheet, unlogged, where the clock runs invisibly
Promising instant auto-response — Leadkaun surfaces and alerts; a human still makes contact

faqs.q: What's a good lead response time?
faqs.a: Faster than most teams manage for Grade A — reaching a hot lead within the hour consistently beats a next-day callback. Lower grades can wait longer, which is the point of grading first.

faqs.q: Does Leadkaun auto-reply to leads?
faqs.a: No. It surfaces the hot lead and alerts the rep so a human responds fast; it does not send automated replies.

faqs.q: How do I actually measure speed-to-lead?
faqs.a: Leadkaun records time-to-first-contact on each lead from the first logged call or WhatsApp exchange, and rolls it up per rep so you can coach the number.

title: How to Recover Cold Leads Before They're Gone
tldr: A cold lead isn't a dead lead — it's an un-worked one. Let stale leads surface themselves with a rupee value, work recovery by grade and ₹ at risk (not by age), reach out and log the outcome (which clears the lead from the missed list), and review recovered ₹ every week. Leadkaun surfaces and reminds — a rep still makes the call.
why: Teams keep buying new leads while the ones they already paid for quietly age out. Without a system, nobody sees the leak: a Grade A that went silent three days ago is worth more than a fresh cold enquiry, but it's invisible in a normal CRM. Recovering stale leads is the cheapest pipeline you will ever add.
prerequisites: Leads graded A–F (ICP configured)
Agreement on the grade-based follow-up windows
A weekly recovery slot in the calendar

steps.heading: Let stale leads surface themselves
steps.body: The Missed Opportunity Engine flags a lead once it passes its grade's follow-up window (Grade A after about a day, B two days, C a week, D a month) with no logged activity — so you don't hunt for cold leads manually.

steps.heading: Put a rupee value on each
steps.body: Every missed lead carries its expected value, and the '₹ at risk today' total is the size of the leak in rupees — the number that makes recovery a priority, not a chore.

steps.heading: Work recovery by grade and rupees, not age
steps.body: Sort the recovery queue by grade and ₹ at risk. One stale Grade A worth ₹5L beats ten cold Grade D enquiries — chase the value, not the oldest row.

steps.heading: Reach out and log it
steps.body: Make contact by call or WhatsApp and log the outcome in 3 taps. Logging activity on a missed lead clears it from the missed list — that is the recovery path — and re-scores it as intent updates.

steps.heading: Catch them before they go fully cold
steps.body: An at-risk alert fires before a lead crosses its deadline, and the 8:30 AM IST Morning Brief lists Grade A/B leads at risk — so you act the same morning instead of at month-end.

steps.heading: Measure recovered ₹ weekly
steps.body: The 'recovered this week' figure totals the won value of previously-stale leads. Put it in your weekly review so recovery becomes a habit with a scoreboard.

commonMistakes: Treating every cold lead equally — grade and ₹ at risk decide the order
Waiting until a lead is fully cold — act on the at-risk alert, not the post-mortem
Not logging the recovery attempt — an unlogged call leaves the lead marked 'missed'
Assuming Leadkaun re-contacts leads for you — it surfaces and values them; a rep makes contact

faqs.q: What counts as a cold or 'missed' lead?
faqs.a: A lead that has passed its grade's follow-up window with no logged activity — Grade A after roughly a day, D after a month. The windows scale with how hot the grade is.

faqs.q: Does Leadkaun re-engage cold leads automatically?
faqs.a: No. It surfaces each stale lead with a rupee value and reminds the rep; the rep makes contact and logs the outcome, which clears it from the missed list.

faqs.q: How is the ₹ at risk calculated?
faqs.a: Each stale lead's expected value, summed across all missed leads, gives the daily ₹-at-risk total.

title: How to Find Where You're Losing Deals in Your Pipeline
tldr: Losing deals feels random until you make it visible. Track where leads go stale by grade and stage, why deals are lost (price, competitor, no response), and which rep and source the ₹ leaks from — then fix the biggest leak first. Leadkaun turns 'we're losing deals' into a ranked, rupee-valued list.
why: Most managers know their pipeline is leaking but can't point to where. Is it slow first response? Follow-up drop-off at the proposal stage? One rep? One junk source? Without the breakdown you coach on vibes and the leak continues. Naming the leak in rupees, by rep and by stage, is the first step to closing it.
prerequisites: Leads graded and moving through pipeline stages
Won/lost outcomes logged with a reason
A weekly review slot

steps.heading: See ₹ at risk, not just lead counts
steps.body: The Missed Opportunity Engine puts a rupee value on every stale lead, so 'leaking pipeline' becomes a number you can rank and act on instead of a feeling.

steps.heading: Break the leak down by rep, source and stage
steps.body: Loss Analysis splits the ₹-at-risk pool by rep, by source, and by industry — so you can tell whether it's a rep-discipline problem, a source-quality problem, or a cadence-design problem.

steps.heading: Log why deals are lost
steps.body: Capture a loss reason on every lost deal — price too high, went to competitor, no budget, no response, requirement changed, wrong fit. Patterns emerge within a couple of weeks.

steps.heading: Find the stage where deals stall
steps.body: The pipeline flags how long leads sit in each stage; a pile-up at one stage — often proposal or negotiation — is your real bottleneck.

steps.heading: Fix the biggest leak first
steps.body: If it's slow first response, tighten the SLA; if it's proposal drop-off, add a follow-up cadence; if it's a junk source, cut it. One fix at a time, each measured against ₹ at risk.

steps.heading: Review the number weekly
steps.body: Bring ₹ at risk and the top loss reasons to your Monday review and watch the leak shrink, instead of rediscovering it at quarter-end.

commonMistakes: Treating loss as random — it clusters by stage, rep and source once you look
Not logging loss reasons — no reasons means no patterns to fix
Trying to fix everything at once — rank by ₹ at risk and fix the biggest leak first
Measuring activity instead of where the rupees actually leak

faqs.q: What loss reasons does Leadkaun track?
faqs.a: Price too high, went to competitor, no budget, no response, requirement changed, and wrong fit — plus your own notes on each lost deal.

faqs.q: Can I see losses by rep?
faqs.a: Yes — Loss Analysis breaks the ₹-at-risk pool and lost deals down by rep, by source, and by industry for your weekly one-on-ones.

faqs.q: How is this different from recovering cold leads?
faqs.a: Recovery works stale leads before they die; loss analysis diagnoses why deals die so you fix the underlying pattern.

title: How to Migrate from Salesforce to Leadkaun (in 2–4 Weeks)

Rightsizing from an enterprise CRM to a Sales Behaviour OS — not downgrading. Leadkaun can also run alongside Salesforce if you're not ready to leave.
why: Most Indian SMBs on Salesforce are paying enterprise per-seat pricing plus admin overhead for a platform built for 200+ reps — when their actual bottleneck is 'which lead does the rep call next.' The migration itself isn't the hard part; the export and the psychology are. You're not downgrading; you're rightsizing to the sales-behaviour layer you actually use.

A Leadkaun account (any tier, including Free) and your ICP defined
Buy-in to run both systems in parallel for ~30 days

steps.heading: Week 1: Export from Salesforce
steps.body: Salesforce → Setup → Data → Data Export gives you a scheduled CSV/ZIP of Leads, Contacts, Accounts, Opportunities and Activities; for a large or filtered pull, use Data Loader. This is the most involved export of any CRM — budget a day and check field-level permissions so nothing is silently dropped.

steps.heading: Week 1: Audit down to live leads
steps.body: Separate genuinely live leads (activity in the last 90 days) from the archive. Most SMBs find over half of a long-lived Salesforce org is dead data you don't want to carry over.

steps.heading: Week 2: Onboard Leadkaun
steps.body: Same-day setup wizard: pick your industry for a pre-configured ICP, then import the live leads via CSV. Indian phone and amount formats are parsed on the way in, and every lead is graded A–F on arrival.

steps.heading: Week 2: Run in parallel
steps.body: Keep Salesforce running (read-only is fine) while reps work primarily from Leadkaun's Priority Queue. This is the low-risk path — and if you have compliance reasons to keep Salesforce, Leadkaun simply runs alongside it as the sales-behaviour layer.

steps.heading: Week 3: Train reps and baseline the numbers
steps.body: A 2-hour hands-on session: 3-tap logging, the Priority Queue, the Morning Brief. Baseline rep adoption, first-response time and ₹ recovered so the parallel-run has a scoreboard.

steps.heading: Week 4: Cut over
steps.body: Switch the primary system to Leadkaun. Keep Salesforce read-only for 90 days as a fallback archive; for niche AppExchange integrations you relied on, a CSV export or Zapier bridge covers most gaps.

steps.heading: Day 90: Decide on Salesforce
steps.body: If the parallel-run numbers held — reps actually adopting, response time down, ₹ recovered rising — consolidate and drop the Salesforce seats. If you still need it for a specific workflow, keep a minimal seat count and let Leadkaun run alongside.

Migrating the whole org instead of live leads — you carry years of dead data
Cutting over before the 30-day parallel-run proves the numbers
Assuming you must replace Salesforce day one — Leadkaun can run alongside it first

faqs.q: What about our AppExchange integrations?
faqs.a: Leadkaun keeps integrations lean and India-first (CSV today, with WhatsApp BSP and Google Sheets sync on the roadmap). For niche tools, a CSV export or Zapier bridge covers most gaps — but it won't match AppExchange breadth, which most SMBs don't need.

faqs.q: How is Leadkaun different from Salesforce?
faqs.a: Salesforce records what happened and is built for large, customised orgs; Leadkaun grades every lead A–F, ranks each rep's queue, and surfaces ₹ at risk — the sales-behaviour layer, at flat INR pricing instead of per-seat USD.

title: How to Manage JustDial Leads (When Speed Decides the Deal)

steps.heading: Call fast, top of the queue
steps.body: Because JustDial shares the enquiry with several vendors, speed-to-lead is decisive. Work the Priority Queue top-down and aim to reach Grade A within the hour, while you're still the first caller.

steps.heading: Log the outcome in 3 taps
steps.body: JustDial buyers often move to a call or WhatsApp — log stage, intent and outcome in 3 taps (any WhatsApp account, no API). Intent updates the grade and keeps the queue honest.

steps.heading: Re-import daily
steps.body: Phone-number dedup means re-importing the day's list only adds genuinely new leads. A native JustDial sync is on the roadmap.

commonMistakes: Calling JustDial leads in arrival order — grade and speed decide, not who came in first
Slow first response — on JustDial a faster vendor simply takes the deal
Treating every JustDial enquiry as a real buyer — let the Quality score flag the junk numbers
Importing without an ICP — fit scoring needs it to be useful

faqs.q: Why does speed matter so much for JustDial?
faqs.a: JustDial shares the enquiry with multiple listed vendors at the same time, so the first credible call usually wins. Grading plus a ranked queue helps you reach the best leads fastest.

faqs.q: Does Leadkaun connect to JustDial automatically?
faqs.a: Not yet — today you export JustDial leads to CSV and import them. A native sync is on the roadmap.

faqs.q: How does it handle junk JustDial numbers?
faqs.a: The Quality score (phone validity, data completeness) pushes junk and repeat numbers low, so reps don't burn time on dead leads.

title: How to Manage Facebook Lead Ads Leads (Volume vs Intent)
tldr: Facebook Lead Ads bring cheap volume but plenty of low-intent, incentive-driven and junk-number leads. Export your Lead Ads submissions to CSV, import into Leadkaun, and grade every one A–F so reps chase the real buyers first — and respond fast, because form-fillers cool quickly. Runs alongside your CRM.
why: A Facebook form-fill is a single tap, so the intent behind it varies wildly — a real chunk are curiosity clicks, freebie-hunters or fake numbers. Working them in arrival order burns reps on tyre-kickers. Grading on arrival, plus fast response while the form-fill is warm, turns a noisy paid channel into a ranked queue you can trust.
prerequisites: Access to your Facebook Lead Ads submissions (Meta Lead Center)
ICP configured so fit scoring is meaningful
A Leadkaun account (any tier, including Free)

steps.heading: Export from Meta
steps.body: Download your Facebook Lead Ads form submissions as CSV from Meta's Lead Center (or your ads manager).

steps.heading: Import into Leadkaun
steps.body: Settings → Leads → Import; map name, phone, email and the form's qualifying answers so scoring has signal to work with.

steps.heading: Grade to separate intent from noise
steps.body: Each lead is scored A–F on arrival. Incentive-hunters, junk numbers and thin submissions score low; genuine, in-ICP leads surface as Grade A/B.

steps.heading: Respond fast
steps.body: A form-fill is warmest in the first hour. Alert the assigned rep and work Grade A at the top of the Priority Queue, before the lead forgets they even filled the form.

steps.heading: Log outcomes in 3 taps
steps.body: Many Facebook leads move to WhatsApp — log stage, intent and outcome in 3 taps (any WhatsApp account). Intent updates the grade.

steps.heading: Judge the channel by ₹, not lead count
steps.body: Tag the source on import; source performance shows ₹ won versus volume, so you can judge Facebook Lead Ads by real conversions. A direct Facebook webhook and native sync are on the roadmap; a generic webhook is available today.

commonMistakes: Judging Facebook by raw lead volume instead of ₹ won
Slow response — form-fillers cool within hours
Ignoring the form's qualifying answers, which are strong fit signal
Treating every submission as a buyer — grade first, then chase the real ones

faqs.q: Aren't Facebook leads low quality?
faqs.a: Many are — which is exactly why grading first matters. The Quality and Fit scores push freebie-hunters and junk numbers down, so reps spend their time on the genuine buyers.

faqs.q: How do leads get from Facebook into Leadkaun?
faqs.a: CSV export from Meta's Lead Center today, or a generic webhook. A direct Facebook Lead Ads webhook and native Google Sheets sync are on the roadmap.

faqs.q: Does Leadkaun auto-reply to form-fillers?
faqs.a: No — it surfaces and alerts the rep so a human responds fast; it does not send automated replies.

title: How to Check a Lead List Before You Import It
metaTitle: How to Check a Lead List Before You Import It | Leadkaun
metaDescription: The twenty minutes before an import are the cheapest in the whole process. What to check in a bought or exported lead list, and what each failure actually costs.
why: The most expensive moment in a bad import is the hour after it, when reps start dialling a file nobody looked at. Everything you can learn before that point is close to free — and the things that go wrong are boringly consistent: dead phone numbers, duplicates of leads someone is already working, and rows that were collected so long ago the contact has forgotten the enquiry. None of that is visible once the rows are mixed into the pipeline.
prerequisites: The file itself, as CSV or a Google Sheet
Your ICP — the industries, states, business types and budget bands you actually sell to
Ten minutes with whoever sourced the list

steps.title: Ask where it came from and when it was collected
steps.body: Before opening the file, get two facts from whoever supplied it: the source, and the collection date. Age is the single strongest predictor of connect rate on a bought list, and it is almost never in the file itself. If nobody can answer the second question, treat the whole list as old.

steps.title: Check phone validity, not phone presence
steps.body: A populated phone column tells you nothing. Count how many values are ten digits, start with a valid Indian mobile prefix, and are not obviously repeated placeholder numbers. A file where a third fails this is not a rep-effort problem; it is a file problem, and no amount of dialling fixes it.

steps.title: Count duplicates against what you already have
steps.body: Duplicates inside the file are easy. The expensive ones are duplicates of leads a rep is already working — two people calling the same prospect from different lists is how you lose a deal you were winning. Match on normalised phone, not on name or email.

steps.title: Decide whether it is B2B at all
steps.body: Look at the company column. If most rows are blank or look like individuals, you have a consumer list, whatever it was sold as. That changes what you do with it entirely, and it is better discovered now than after a week of calls.

steps.title: Check fit before quality
steps.body: Take twenty rows at random and ask whether you would want them as customers — sector, size, geography. If the answer is mostly no, the data quality is irrelevant. A clean list of the wrong companies is still the wrong list.

steps.title: Import, then measure by band
steps.body: Once imported, watch connect rate by freshness band and grade distribution by source rather than raw totals. Two lists with identical row counts can differ enormously in what they produce, and this is the only way to tell before the money is spent again.

commonMistakes: Judging a list by row count. Volume is the least informative number in the file.
Treating completeness as quality. A fully-populated row with a fake number is worse than a sparse one with a real decision-maker.
Importing without recording the source, which makes it impossible to tell later which purchase was worth repeating.
Blaming reps for a poor connect rate on a list nobody validated.

faqs.q: Can Leadkaun check the file before I import it?
faqs.a: Yes. It profiles a sample of the file and reports a readiness band — High, Medium or Low — from phone and email validity, field completeness, in-file duplicates and whether the data looks B2B or B2C. The analysis is deterministic arithmetic on formats rather than a model, and it runs while you wait rather than in the background.

faqs.q: What if the list fails the check?
faqs.a: Import it anyway, but knowing what it is. A Low band tells you to expect a poor connect rate and to hold reps to a different standard on it — which is more useful than discovering the same thing over three weeks of calls.

faqs.q: How old is too old?
faqs.a: There is no universal number, and anyone who gives you one is guessing. Measure it: track connect rate by freshness band on your own lists for a quarter, and the threshold where it falls off a cliff is your answer, for your market.
